90301.text: What is the revenue-earning portion of the Traffic Load (passengers, baggage, and cargo carried for remuneration) called?
options: Payload
Variable Load
Dry Operating Mass
Useful Load

90302.text: How is Contingency Fuel (for unforeseen wind, routing, or ATC deviations) determined?
options: The higher of 5% of trip fuel or fuel for 5 minutes of holding at 1,500 ft AGL over the destination aerodrome.
The lower of 10% of alternate fuel or 15 minutes of cruise fuel.
Always 45 minutes of holding fuel for piston aeroplanes and 30 minutes for turbine aeroplanes.
A fixed 10 minutes of taxi fuel added at the commander's discretion.

90303.text: What is the required Final Reserve Fuel (holding at 1,500 ft AGL above the alternate aerodrome) for piston-engine and gas-turbine aeroplanes respectively?
options: 45 minutes for piston aeroplanes and 30 minutes for gas-turbine aeroplanes.
30 minutes for piston aeroplanes and 45 minutes for gas-turbine aeroplanes.
A fixed 20 minutes for both piston and gas-turbine aeroplanes.
60 minutes for piston aeroplanes and 15 minutes for gas-turbine aeroplanes.

90304.text: Which fuel category is added above the mandatory fuel requirements at the discretion of the commander and/or flight dispatcher?
options: Extra fuel
Contingency fuel
Final reserve fuel
Trip fuel

90305.text: In the ICAO Standard Atmosphere (ISA, Doc 7488), what are the sea-level temperature, pressure, air density, and tropospheric temperature lapse rate respectively?

90306.text: Which error correction is applied to Calibrated Airspeed (CAS) at higher speeds (above Mach 0.3 / 300 KTAS) to obtain Equivalent Airspeed (EAS)?
options: Compressibility error
Instrument and position error
Air density error
Wind component correction

90307.text: What speeds are marked by the lower and upper ends of the white arc on an Airspeed Indicator (ASI)?
options: Lower limit VS0 (stalling speed in landing configuration), upper limit VFE (maximum flap extended speed).
Lower limit VS1 (clean stalling speed), upper limit VNO (maximum structural cruising speed).
Lower limit VNO (maximum structural cruising speed), upper limit VNE (never exceed speed).
Lower limit VR (rotation speed), upper limit VLOF (lift-off speed).

90308.text: Which aeroplanes belong to Performance Class B?
options: Single- or multi-engine propeller aeroplanes with a maximum passenger seating configuration of 9 or fewer and MTOM of 5,700 kg or less.
All multi-engine jet and turboprop aeroplanes with 10 or more passenger seats or MTOM above 5,700 kg.
Multi-engine piston propeller aeroplanes with 10 or more passenger seats or MTOM above 5,700 kg.
Only heavy commercial transport aeroplanes above 136,000 kg MTOM.

90309.text: What is the take-off screen height to be reached at the end of the take-off distance for Performance Class A and Class B aeroplanes respectively?
options: 35 ft for Class A, 50 ft for Class B
50 ft for Class A, 35 ft for Class B
15 ft for both Class A and Class B
100 ft for Class A, 50 ft for Class B

90310.text: How does take-off decision speed (V1) change on a wet runway compared to a dry runway, and what is its required relationship with minimum control speed on the ground (VMCG)?
options: V1 decreases because stopping distance increases; VMCG must always be less than or equal to V1 (VMCG ≤ V1).
V1 increases because stopping distance decreases; V1 must always be less than VMCG.
A wet runway does not affect V1; VMCG applies only during landing.
On a wet runway V1 increases above VR.

90311.text: As a regulatory safety margin against wind variations during take-off performance calculations, what percentages of reported headwind and tailwind components must be factored?
options: Not more than 50% of the headwind component and not less than 150% of the tailwind component.
Not less than 150% of the headwind component and not more than 50% of the tailwind component.
Exactly 100% of both headwind and tailwind components.
75% of the headwind component, while tailwind components are ignored.

90312.text: Comparing Climb-Limited Take-Off Mass (CLTOM) and Obstacle-Limited Take-Off Mass (OLTOM), what is the effect of a tailwind?
options: A tailwind does not affect CLTOM, but it reduces OLTOM because it flattens the ground climb gradient.
A tailwind increases both CLTOM and OLTOM by the same amount.
A tailwind reduces CLTOM but has no effect on OLTOM.
A tailwind affects neither CLTOM nor OLTOM.

90313.text: In an ICAO ATS flight plan, up to which point is Total Estimated Elapsed Time (Total EET) calculated for VFR and IFR flights respectively?
options: For VFR, from take-off to arrival over the destination aerodrome; for IFR, from take-off to the Initial Approach Fix (IAF) of the destination aerodrome.
For both VFR and IFR, from engine start-up to engine shut-down at the parking stand.
For VFR, cruise time only; for IFR, total time including diversion to the alternate aerodrome.
For VFR, from take-off to the IAF; for IFR, from take-off to touchdown.

90314.text: What is the primary structural purpose of the Maximum Zero Fuel Mass (MZFM) limitation?
options: To prevent excessive wing root bending moments caused by fuselage load when wing fuel tanks are empty.
To prevent overheating of the main landing gear shock struts on touchdown.
To limit fuel uplift so thermal expansion space remains in the fuel tanks.
To prevent excessive brake temperatures during taxi.

90315.text: Given MSTOM = 65,000 kg, PLTOM = 68,000 kg, MSLM = 59,000 kg, PLLM = 57,500 kg, MZFM = 53,000 kg, take-off fuel (TOF) = 11,000 kg, and trip fuel = 5,500 kg, what is the maximum allowable take-off mass (MTOM)?

90316.text: An aeroplane has a Mean Aerodynamic Chord (MAC) length of 2.00 m, its leading edge (LeMAC) is 12.40 m aft of the datum, and the CG is at 12.90 m aft of the datum. What is the CG position in %MAC?
options: 25% MAC
20% MAC
40% MAC
50% MAC

90317.text: If a heavy cargo item with a small base exceeds the cargo compartment's area (floor) load limit (kg/m²), what must be done to load it safely?
options: Use load spreaders (planks/plates) to distribute the mass over a larger floor area.
Place a narrow support under its centre to concentrate the weight at one point.
Ignore the area load limit as long as total compartment mass is not exceeded.
Lean the cargo against the fuselage sidewall to keep it off the floor.
